constitution: PR #1641 — Wheel of Football grading constitution
gradingSemantic: CURRENT NFL ABILITY AT QUARTERBACK RIGHT NOW; position-normalized; stable against ordinary weekly noise; not career greatness, fame, fantasy value, draft status, projection, or a one/two-game hot streak.

evidenceSnapshot.note: Week 4 was not complete. Most current-season evidence reflects 2-3 games; Pittsburgh/Cleveland had four. 2025 full-season evidence and prior established level are intentionally weighted more heavily than ordinary September noise.
primarySources: NFL.com Next Gen Stats context embedded in the Week 4 QB Index

grades.reason: Current ceiling: complete passing/creation/rushing profile; one early-2026 turnover game is ordinary noise, not a level change.
Elite processing, arm talent and creation remain established; 2026 start is again high-end, but 2025 prevents a reputation-only 99/100.
Elite passer plus unmatched quarterback rushing stress; current dual-threat level remains just below the absolute ceiling.
2025 MVP and elite full-season passing baseline; early pressure struggles in 2026 are too small a sample for a major downgrade.
Elite placement, processing and pocket passing with a strong 2026 start; no meaningful current gap from Stafford.
Established high-end current starter with strong 2025 efficiency/QBR and a clean 2026 opening stretch.
2025 was legitimately elite and MVP-caliber; the disastrous three-game 2026 opening is meaningful enough to lower him, but not enough to erase the established level.
Efficient 2024-25 passing plus major designed/rushing value; early-2026 indecision and uneven play keep him below the elite anchors.
Very good current quarterback whose 2026 heater is real evidence but not enough to promote him into the Dak/elite neighborhood after a more mixed prior sample.
Excellent structured operator with sustained efficiency; narrower off-platform and pressure creation keeps him below the high-end ceiling.
Top physical toolkit remains, but 2025 and early-2026 mistakes/volatility do not support grading the idea of Herbert above his actual recent quarterback play.
Meaningful 2025 step forward with a good 2026 start; still too much historical inconsistency for the high-end band.
Special rushing/creation ability and a proven high-end rookie season remain real; shortened and less efficient 2025-26 evidence prevents a higher current grade.
Three strong established starter seasons through 2025 outweigh a rough three-game 2026 opening, but the current inconsistency caps him here.
2024 showed a high ceiling, while 2025 and the 2026 opening regressed; current thumb availability is an eligibility issue, not an ability penalty.
Still a good current starter, but 2024-26 performance has not sustained his rookie-year peak; safe play and middling recent efficiency cap the grade.
Two straight credible starting seasons with strong efficiency; turnover volatility keeps him at the solid/above-average anchor rather than the high-end group.
2025 was turnover-heavy, while his 2026 opening has been sharp; the combined current body supports a solid starter just below Darnold.
Clear development in 2025, especially reducing sacks, plus real creation ability; accuracy/consistency remain uneven enough to stay below the 85 anchor.
Established dual-threat ability remains above replacement-level starter quality; small recent samples are weak, while injury/availability is kept separate from ability.
Strong 2025 resurgence is real, but early 2026 regression plus a long prior record of volatility prevents treating that season as a fully established new level.
Excellent three-game 2026 start earns respect, but the post-Achilles recent baseline and reduced movement/arm margin prevent a recency-driven jump.
Positive 2025 starter sample with meaningful rushing value and a strong two-game 2026 start; still too little NFL evidence for a larger move.
The approved average/solid starter line: competent, stable NFL quarterbacking without high-end creation or sustained difference-making.
Thirteen-game body shows credible starter-level efficiency and enough mobility; ball-security volatility keeps him at the Brissett line.
Early 2026 improvement is encouraging and materially better than his prior baseline, but three games do not yet justify moving above the established starter line.
Two full seasons of competent but low-efficiency play plus a shaky 2026 opening place him just below the average-starter anchor.
Four-game 2026 rebound is enough for a small current upgrade, but the poor 2022-24 NFL sample and 2025 absence block a larger recency-driven move.
Below-average current starter anchor: still capable of high-level pocket stretches, but 2025 and 2026 efficiency no longer support an above-average grade.
Arm/timing flashes are evident, but fifteen total NFL games and an 86.8 career passer rating provide limited proof of better than below-average starter ability.
Physical/rushing tools and strong prior spot starts remain useful, but his 2026 starter sample shows accuracy and drive-finishing limitations.
A full 2025 season and early 2026 both show below-average efficiency; enough arm talent and creation keep him above the weakest Wheel options.
No regular-season NFL snaps. Promising flashes were offset by a rough preseason and losing the starting job to Cousins; grade is deliberately provisional and contains no draft-slot projection bonus.
Weak current Wheel option anchor: NFL arm talent still creates plays, but current reliability, efficiency and decision volatility are clearly below the starter line.

resolvedPressurePoints: Purdy and Herbert remain at the user-approved corrected anchor values (89 and 88); neither receives a trait/reputation or three-game-hot-streak premium.
Maye stays above Purdy/Goff because the 2025 MVP-caliber season remains the strongest established evidence, but falls well below the elite anchors because the 2026 collapse is too severe to ignore.
Hurts is tied with Maye at 90: his rushing value and 2024-25 efficiency remain high-end, while current passing indecision prevents a 92+ placement.
Trevor Lawrence, Jayden Daniels and Jordan Love tie at 87 for different reasons; the audit found no defensible full-point separation in current overall quarterback ability.
Darnold remains the approved 85 anchor despite strong efficiency because turnover volatility is persistent and the grade is ability, not team record.
Mendoza receives a provisional 75 rather than a projection-based rookie premium; first meaningful regular-season snaps should trigger a targeted review.

postGradeDistribution.note: Distribution was inspected only after player-by-player grading and did not drive any grade.

runtimeBoundary: No production/runtime grading behavior is changed by this artifact. Phase 5 will wire server-owned grades, frozen historical selection grades, and hidden reveal behavior separately.
futureVersioning: Any future grade change must record previous grade, new grade, effective date, concise reason, and nearby anchor/peer sanity check.
